title: BRP: Query-Efficient Block Revert Patch for Decision-Based Black-Box Adversarial Attack

problem.claim: Decision-based black-box adversarial patch attacks must generate effective localized perturbations when only predicted labels are observable.

gap.claim: Existing decision-based adversarial patch attacks are underexplored and often have low query efficiency and large patch areas.

contributions.claim: BRP formulates adversarial patch generation as a pixel-block reversion problem using a two-stage progressive refinement process.
The single-block revert test identifies blocks whose reversion preserves the adversarial effect, and global revert optimization searches combinations of those blocks to reduce patch size.
BRP alternates the two stages in a coarse-to-fine refinement process.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present BRP as a novel reverse construction method for query-efficient adversarial patch generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments show BRP significantly reduces patch size and query cost compared with state-of-the-art decision-based attacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Adversarial patches can control deep neural network predictions with small localized perturbations.
Decision-based black-box attacks are framed as realistic and challenging because attackers observe only predicted labels.
Decision-based adversarial patch attacks are underexplored, while existing methods face query-efficiency and patch-area limitations.
BRP reverses pixel blocks through single-block testing and global combination optimization, alternating the stages for coarse-to-fine refinement.
Experiments are reported to show lower patch size and query cost than state-of-the-art decision-based attacks.
